properties.html: Ravi and Raju have a race where they are going to run from point A to B, turn around and run back to point A, where AB = 100 metres. Their speeds are constant but are not the same. Further, they both run twice as fast from B to A as from A to B. On Ravi’s return journey from B to A, he meets Raju at a distance of 200/11 metres from B. The difference in the time taken by each of them to complete the whole race is 12.5 seconds. How long (in seconds) does Raju take to complete the race?

properties.html:
A factory starts a certain manufacturing job on August 1, 2009. The job involves seven processes: A, B, C, D, E, F and G. Initially, only processes D and E can be started; D takes 12 days for completion, while E requires only 7 days. Process B, which requires 5 days, can be started only after both D and E are finished. Process C, which takes 8 days, can be started after E is completed. Process F, which requires 5 days, can be started only after D and C finish. Process G, which takes 2 days, may commence only after B and C are over. Process A, lasting 6 days, can commence only after all the other processes end. Processes can be carried out simultaneously.

If there are six extra workers who can be deployed for process C and A, there by halving the time for these processes, then which is the earliest date on which the project could now be completed?
